docs.task: How the runner's slot limiter caps concurrent executions per workspace.

asks: Explain how the runner's slot limiter caps concurrent executions per workspace.

data_flow.step: The planner returns `Step::Spawn(req)` steps from the session's fold. `drive` inserts each step key into `Live.inflight` and spawns a tokio task per new key.
`perform` matches `Step::Spawn(req)` and calls `perform_spawn`. This is the only caller of `perform_spawn`. `Step::Judge` goes to `perform_judge` and takes no slot.

`perform_spawn` first awaits `acquire_slot()`. The loop re-reads `limits.max_parallel_executions` from the live workspace settings, compares it with `slots`, and either increments and returns a `Slot` or waits up to 2 s for `slot_free` and retries. No event is appended while it waits (none is appended in `acquire_slot` or before it in `perform_spawn`).

With the slot held, `perform_spawn` snapshots the session. If the session is terminal or paused, or the explore task was abandoned while waiting (Rule U1), it returns `Ok(())` and the local `slot` drops, freeing the count with nothing started.

Otherwise it records the execution as running, creates the `EngineHost` with `slot: Mutex::new(Some(slot))`, and awaits `executor.run(spec, host.clone(), token)`. The slot is held for the whole run, for native and harness executors alike.
A harness run that asks another subagent calls `EngineHost::wait_for_wake`, which drops its slot, awaits its message, then calls `acquire_slot` again and stores the new slot (Rule H2).

After the run, `perform_spawn` appends `ExecutionFinished` (and a `SecurityBlock` if a review set one), then `drop(lock(&host.slot).take())` releases the slot. `Slot::drop` decrements `slots` and calls `slot_free.notify_waiters()`, waking waiting spawns, which also poll every 2 s.

patterns.description: The limiter is not a semaphore. `Inner.slots` is a `Mutex<usize>` of executions currently holding a slot and `slot_free` is a `tokio::sync::Notify`. `acquire_slot` loops: it reads the limit fresh from `self.services.workspace().limits.max_parallel_executions` (clamped with `.max(1)`), takes the std mutex, and if the count is below the limit increments it and returns a `Slot`. Otherwise it waits on `slot_free.notified()` with a 2-second timeout and loops again. `Slot` holds an `Arc<Inner>`; its `Drop` decrements the counter with `saturating_sub(1)` and calls `notify_waiters()`, so release happens on success, error, cancellation or panic. The mutex guard is dropped before any `.await`. The limit value is never stored, only compared, so a settings change applies to waiting spawns and never cancels running ones.
patterns.name: Counter plus Notify slot guard

patterns.description: `perform_spawn` moves the `Slot` into `EngineHost.slot: Mutex<Option<Slot>>`. The host, not the spawn function, owns it while the executor runs, so `wait_for_wake` can `take()` it out (Rule H2) and put a new one in after `acquire_slot().await`. After `ExecutionFinished` is appended, `perform_spawn` drops the slot explicitly. Hosts for inspect and quick-answer runs are built with `slot: Mutex::new(None)`.
patterns.name: Slot handed to the execution host so the executor can release it

patterns.description: `next_steps` is pure and `PlanCtx` carries only the budget and format commands, not the parallel limit. `drive` starts a tokio task for every new step key, and each `Step::Spawn` task blocks inside `perform_spawn` at `acquire_slot`. So a stage that plans N spawns creates N tasks immediately, of which at most `limit` proceed. The step key stays in `inflight` while a task waits, so the waiting spawn is not started twice.
patterns.name: Planner is unaware of the limit; the runner throttles

submit.findings_summary: The limiter is a `Mutex<usize>` counter plus a `Notify` on `Inner` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`. Each workspace has one Engine, so the cap applies per workspace across all its sessions. `acquire_slot` re-reads `limits.max_parallel_executions` (default 3, clamped to at least 1, 0 rejected at save) on every loop and polls every 2 s. `perform_spawn` is the only caller that takes a slot for a planned spawn. The `Slot` guard frees the count on drop and is handed to `EngineHost` so a waiting harness run can release and re-acquire it (Rule H2). Judges, quick answers and inspect runs hold no slot. The counter has no project or session key, and only one test uses the limit (set to 1, for H2).

docs.task: How project entries in workspace settings are defined and validated, and how the runner knows a spawn's project.

asks: How project entries in workspace settings are defined
How the runner knows which project a spawn belongs to

data_flow.step: The user edits settings. `workspace.toml` deserializes into `WorkspaceSettings` (`#[serde(default)]`), so `projects` is a list of `ProjectEntry` (`[[projects]]` tables).

Save or live check: `WorkspaceRt::validate` calls `validate_settings`, which runs `ostra_sandbox::validate::workspace`, then `validate_workspace` (key syntax, key uniqueness, absolute path, stack text, code provider command and timeout 1-120, language server command, languages from `code::NAV_LANGUAGES`, one server per language, timeout 1-120, routes, MCP, limits), then permission-rule parsing, then the folder-exists check (`p.path.is_absolute() && !p.path.is_dir()`). `WorkspaceRt::validate` adds instruction tag checks (Rule W3). The REST endpoint `validate_workspace` returns the issues without saving.

`save_settings` returns `Err(issues)` when any issue exists; otherwise it writes through `trust::save_workspace` and calls `sync_projects`, which upserts a `ProjectRow` (key, path, init status from whether the project's inventory file exists) and deletes rows for removed keys.

A session starts: `start_session` reads `services.workspace()` and maps every `ProjectEntry` to `ProjectRef { key, path }`. For a pipeline session it keeps only projects whose inventory exists, rejects unknown pinned keys, and keeps only pinned ones (Rule O6). The list is written into the session-created event.

The fold stores the list in `SessionState.projects` (and `scope` for init sessions). From then on the session sees the project list as it was at creation, not later edits to settings. `ProjectCreated` can append a project (Rule O3).

The pure planner emits `Step::Spawn(Box<SpawnRequest>)`; `Planner::spawn` fills `project` from its `project: &str` argument (cross-project stages use `SessionState::primary()`, per-project stages use that project's key). The `Step::key()` guards against double start.
The driver loop calls `next_steps(&st, &plan_ctx)`, inserts each step key into `inflight`, and runs `perform` in its own tokio task. `Step::Spawn` goes to `perform_spawn`.

`perform_spawn` first awaits `acquire_slot()` (workspace-wide), then snapshots state, resolves the route, and resolves `repo_root`: the session dir when the implementer creates a project (Rule O2), otherwise `st.project_path(&req.project)`, falling back to the workspace root when the key is not in the session list.

The runner loads that project's `project.toml` and inventory, builds the spawn through the factory, appends `ExecutionStarted { project: req.project.clone(), ... }` (folded into `ExecRecord.project`), inserts the db row with the same project, and builds `ExecContext { project_key: req.project.clone(), repo_root, ... }` for the executor. The slot moves into `EngineHost.slot` and is freed when the host drops it or the run waits for a message.

document.problem: A workspace lists projects in `workspace.toml` as `ProjectEntry` values. Settings are checked at save time by `validate_workspace` plus extra checks in `ostra-workspace`. Every spawn carries a project key chosen by the planner, and the runner resolves that key to a folder through the session's frozen project list. The only concurrency cap today is one counter per workspace (`limits.max_parallel_executions`), which does not look at the spawn's project.
